item.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of P2P Direct Connection and Tunneling across Complex Network Environments
item.description: The three earlier posts in this series covered the landscape (the survey), the RDP protocol itself (the deep dive), and product comparisons (the comparison); P2P protocol theory was dissected in the P2P signaling and relay survey. One layer remains: the network environment itself. The same STUN/TURN/ICE machinery, dropped into different network constraints, yields entirely different hole-punch success rates, viable solutions, and experience floors — CGNAT-dense access networks, UDP-hostile paths, carriers with uneven peering, congested long-distance backbones at peak. These constraints combine very differently across networks, and selection logic must follow the environment rather than any template.
